data.name: Eliathah
data.gender_notes: Eliathah is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The Hebrew name Eliathah is derived from the Hebrew elements El (My God) and Yah (YHWH, the Hebrew name for God). It is a Hebrew name borne by several characters in the Old Testament. Eliathah is also the name of one of the sons of Saul and Rizpah (2 Samuel 21:8). The name Eliathah carries the meaning “My God is Yah” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Eliathah usually hope their child will grow to embody my god is yah and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Reflects one's deep faith and devotion to God.
data.etymology: Eliathah belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “My God is Yah.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Eliathah total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_hebrew.name: אליעתה
in_hebrew.meaning: אלוהים הוא האל שלי, ה' הוא המושיע שלי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אליעתה הוא שם פרטי עברי המורכב מ'אל' ו'יעתה', שפירושו 'אלוהים הוא האל שלי' או 'ה' הוא המושיע שלי'. השם מופיע בתנ'ך, ביחזקאל ובדברי הימים, ומשמעותו רוחנית ועמוקה, הקושרת בין האדם לאלוהים.

in_greek.name: Ελιαθας
in_greek.meaning: Ο Θεός είναι ο Θεός μου
in_greek.long_meaning: Ελιαθας είναι ένα όνομα που προέρχεται από την Εβραϊκή γλώσσα και σημαίνει 'Ο Θεός είναι ο Θεός μου' ή 'Ο Κύριος είναι ο σωτήρας μου'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, παρόμοια ονόματα αναφέρονται ως σύμβολο της πίστης και της αφοσίωσης στον Θεό.

in_latin.name: Eliathah

Historically, it reflects the monotheistic beliefs of the Israelites and early Christians. The name symbolizes faith, spiritual strength, and divine protection.

biblical_reference.note: A leader of the Levites during David's reign.

historical_references.reference: According to the Old Testament book of 1 Samuel, Eliathah was a priest who ministered in the Tabernacle at Shiloh during the time of the judges. He is mentioned as the father of Iddo, who in turn was the father of the high priest Azariah during the reign of King Josiah of Judah (around 640 BCE).
historical_references.context: Pre-monarchic period of Israelite history, during the time of the judges.

historical_references.reference: In the New Testament apocryphal book of the Shepherd of Hermas, the name Eliathah is given to the angelic guide who leads the protagonist Hermas through a series of visions and interpretations of allegorical dreams. The book was likely written around the late 2nd century CE.
